answers.flag: Option D (Elastic) is defensible because the stem gives no throughput figure, so cost versus Provisioned cannot be computed and Elastic is often the default recommendation; only the cues 'steady-state, predictable, close to its peak all day' favor B.

case.label: D
case.text: Elastic throughput restores performance immediately with no capacity planning and no risk of under-provisioning, and AWS now steers most workloads to it. The stem never states the actual MiB/s or the monthly data transferred, so a candidate cannot prove that per-GB Elastic charges exceed the cost of provisioned MiB/s above the included baseline. With only 100 GiB stored, the Provisioned charge for the peak rate could plausibly be high while Elastic pricing for a modest workload could be lower. The decisive cues (steady, predictable, near peak all day) are what make B right, and they are also nearly a giveaway of the key.
